hero.sub: A dripping showerhead, a handle that won't turn or water that swings from hot to cold. We repair shower valves, cartridges, heads and drains, with a flat price before we start. Serving Highland Park and the North Shore.

blocks.intro: Most shower problems come from the valve behind the wall, not the parts you can see:

tiles.body: A worn cartridge or washer in the valve lets water through even when the handle is off.
Water that runs hot then cold, or never gets hot, points to a worn cartridge or a failing pressure-balancing valve.
A clogged showerhead is easy. If the whole bathroom is weak, older pipes or a partly closed valve may be the cause.
Handles that are hard to turn, spin freely or broke off usually need a new cartridge or stem.

blocks.h2: Shower Repairs in Older Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and many bathrooms still have their original shower valves behind the tile.

items.body: Older valves can still be repaired, but parts can be harder to find. We'll tell you if a repair will hold or if replacing the valve makes more sense.
Galvanized water lines narrow with corrosion over the decades. If pressure is weak at every fixture, the pipes may be the real problem.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: We fix the shower without turning it into a remodel you didn't ask for.

steps.body: Your plumber explains what's wrong in plain English first, then walks you through your options. You decide.

steps.h3: 2. A Clear Price Before Any Work Starts
steps.body: You get a flat-rate price before we touch anything, with no surprise add-ons when the job is done.
Shoe covers on, work area protected, and the space cleaned up before we leave.

blocks.h2: Shower Repair Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Why does my shower keep dripping after I turn it off?
items.preview: A worn part in the valve. Replacing it usually fixes it without opening the wall.
items.answer: A worn cartridge, washer or seat inside the valve lets water through. Replacing the worn part usually fixes it without opening the wall.

items.q: Can you replace a shower valve without tearing out the tile?
items.preview: Often, yes. Many repairs are done through the trim opening.
items.answer: Often, yes. Many repairs are done through the trim opening. A full valve replacement sometimes needs access from behind or a larger trim plate. We'll explain before we start.

items.q: Why does my shower go from hot to cold?
items.preview: Usually a worn cartridge or pressure-balancing valve, sometimes the water heater.
items.answer: Usually a worn cartridge or a pressure-balancing valve that isn't keeping up when another fixture is used. It can also be a water heater problem. See [water heater repair](/highland-park/water-heater-repair).

items.q: How much does shower repair cost?
items.preview: It depends on the valve and parts. You get a flat price before any work begins.
items.answer: It depends on the valve type, the parts it needs and access behind the wall. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
